News Contact Network Orchestration How OpenGlobe solutions are transforming enterprise IT infrastructure Introduction Automation and orchestration are terms often used in the context of networks, but they have important nuances that set them apart. While both aim to optimize processes and increase efficiency, their focuses are distinct. Network automation focuses on automating individual and repetitive tasks, such as configuring devices, troubleshooting simple issues, and collecting data. It’s like teaching a robot to tighten a screw: a specific and well-defined task. By eliminating the need for manual intervention, automation reduces execution time, minimizes errors, and frees IT professionals for more strategic activities. Network orchestration, on the other hand, goes further by coordinating multiple tasks and services to manage complex workflows. It’s like conducting an orchestra: each instrument (service) needs to play at the right time and with the appropriate intensity to create perfect harmony. Orchestration enables the automation of processes such as deploying new applications, provisioning network resources, configuring firewalls, and load balancing in an integrated and consistent manner. In summary, automation provides the foundation for orchestration. By automating individual tasks, it’s possible to create building blocks that can be orchestrated into more complex processes. A revolution in the way we build and manage networks Introduction to Open Networking Open Networking represents a fundamental shift in the way networks are built and managed. It is an approach that separates hardware from software, enabling greater flexibility, innovation and cost-effectiveness. Fundamental Concepts ONIE (Open Network Install Environment) It is a bootable installer that allows automatic installation of any compatible network operating system on a barebones network switch. NOS (Network Operating System) Specialized operating system for network equipment, which can be chosen independently of the hardware. Success Story: Facebook Wedge The Edgecore Wedge-16X represents a milestone in the history of Open Networking, being the first commercial product based on Facebook’s Wedge design. News Contact Unlocking the Power of Open Networking: OpenGlobe’s Revolution in the Networking Industry Introduction In today’s rapidly evolving technology, the demand for more flexible, scalable, and cost-effective networks has never been higher. Enter OpenGlobe, a pioneering company that is redefining the future of networking with its innovative open networking solutions. In this article, we’ll dive into the world of open networking and explore how OpenGlobe is leading this revolution. What is open network? https://openglobe.io/ Before we dive into OpenGlobe’s solutions, it’s crucial to understand the concept of open networking. Open networking, also known as Open Networking, is an approach to network design, construction, and management that emphasizes interoperability, flexibility, and freedom of choice. Unlike traditional networks, which often rely on proprietary hardware and software from a single vendor, open networks utilize open standards and programmable interfaces. Main features of the open network: Hardware and software disaggregation :Hardware and software can be purchased separately, allowing for greater flexibility. Interoperability : Equipment from different manufacturers can work together harmoniously. Programmability : Networks can be easily customized and automated through programming interfaces. Economy : Competition between suppliers and flexibility of choice often result in lower costs.
